text:
**9,400 metres.** That is how deep the Marisol Trench probe went, according to the Halvern Deep-Sea Institute.

The probe reached maximum depth on 14 March 2031 and transmitted its final reading. The descent took 6 hours 52 minutes.

The figures appear in the Institute's "Marisol Trench Descent Report (Mission MT-7)", released at a press briefing on 16 March 2031. Dr. Ilvane Corsetti, lead mission oceanographer, presented the findings.

**What it means for the sector:** A completed descent to 9,400 metres, with data returned at the end, gives deep-sea equipment makers a concrete benchmark. Survey and sensor suppliers will likely cite MT-7 when pitching for work at extreme depth. Buyers are likely to start asking for comparable proof of performance.
